paragraphs.source_en: Having recovered his true mettle as a samurai, Shirojiro now had one paramount task: to investigate Hideyoshi's military dispositions around Osaka. Through his eyes, Ieyasu could learn when and where Hideyoshi would mobilize his main force and thus make a reasonably accurate judgment. Hideyoshi, who advocated positional warfare at every turn, would never venture into Mino unless his own stronghold was secure.

paragraphs.source_en: “Well...” Shirojiro grew tense. “Judging from Hideyoshi's decision to send Nakamura Kazuuji to Kishiwada Castle, I believe the defense of Osaka will most likely be entrusted to Hachisuka Hikoemon Masakatsu.”
